ce_bugs.text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Each collective host's Office365 credential still targets the first host's calendar, so secondary-host event creation can fail or write into the wrong calendar.

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:162 — CalDAV-style collective creations filter every host credential's calendars using only the first destination calendar, silently skipping secondary hosts' calendars.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — Google Meet bookings without a destination calendar now dereference an undefined first calendar and fail before fallback.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1077 — Collective bookings with no event-type or organizer destination calendar discard every other host's destination calendar because the optional push targets null.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — Google Meet bookings without a destination calendar now dereference `undefined.integration` and abort event creation instead of falling back to Cal Video.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254 — Calendar updates with no saved externalCalendarId pass an undefined calendarId because the new fallback searches for an undefined id, causing Google update requests to fail.

mrv_findings.text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254 — `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` searches for `undefined` when no external ID is supplied, so Google updates receive no destination calendar ID.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:168 — `calendarId: selectedCalendar,` omits the `"primary"` fallback used for insertion, so the Meet-description patch sends an invalid Google Calendar request when no destination matches.
docs/tasks/task-001.md:2 — `Review the change.` supplies no acceptance criteria or verification for collective multi-host creation, update, cancellation, and rescheduling.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),` changes organization slug persistence unrelated to the destination-calendar task and can alter organization creation.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar") {` dereferences `undefined.integration` for empty/omitted destination calendars, crashing Meet bookings before calendar/video creation.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:375 — `const destinationCalendarCredentials = this.calendarCredentials.filter((c) => c.type === destination.integration);` discards a credential-less destination's external ID, so Google falls back to each credential's primary calendar and creates events in the wrong calendars.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:142 — `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` followed by `calendarId: selectedCalendar` targets `undefined` in the Meet-link patch after an insert into primary, leaving the event update invalid or mismatched.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...` and `email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` uses the first host's calendar address for every per-host event, misrepresenting later hosts' organizer identity.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),` reverses team-billing slug behavior without acceptance in the stated destination-calendar objective.
apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249 — `destinationCalendar: [],` only updates a no-destination rejected-webhook fixture, so it can pass without exercising collective multi-host routing.
